drivingQuestion: Why does the mitzva of sending away the mother bird not apply to sacrificial birds?
outcomeNote: the mishna's exclusion of consecrated birds is grounded in the wording of Deuteronomy 22:7

segments.he: בְּחוּלִּין אֲבָל לֹא בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁים. אַמַּאי לָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח אֶת הָאֵם״ – בְּמִי שֶׁאַתָּה מְצוֶּּוה לְשַׁלְּחוֹ, יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מְצוֶּּוה לְשַׁלְּחוֹ אֶלָּא לַהֲבִיאוֹ לִידֵי גִּזְבָּר.
segments.en: § The mishna states that the mitzva of sending away the mother bird from the nest applies «to non-sacred» birds, «but not to sacrificial» birds. The Gemara asks: «Why» does this mitzva «not» apply to sacrificial birds? The Gemara responds: «As the verse states: “You shall send the mother”» (Deuteronomy 22:7). The verse refers only «to» a bird «that you are commanded to send» away, i.e., a non-sacred bird; that «excludes this» sacrificial bird, «which you are not commanded to send» away, but «rather to bring it to the custody of» the Temple «treasurer.»
